name: Sur
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Benard Abraham & Innocent Jonah. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Kusur-Myet (Sur) [tdl] Language of Plateau and Bauchi States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-023. SIL International. 49 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.2 Phonology (pp. 10-11) gives tentative consonant and vowel inventories and labialization/palatalization notes; states 'there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological features'; wordlist appendix repeats that transcriptions are preliminary with no tone analysis. No mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006. The Sur (Tapshin) language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Ms., Mallam Dendo, Cambridge (printout 25 April 2006), 27 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology gives vowel and consonant charts (pp. 3-4); sec. 3.3 'Tones' is an empty heading; intro p. 2: 'In general, tones are not marked.' No mention of stress or accent anywhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2004. Tarok and related languages of East-Central Nigeria: nomenclature and subclassification. Ms. (printout 22 Oct 2004).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; sec. 3.3 Phonology is comparative proto-Tarokoid vowel/consonant correspondences with Sur forms cited; tone remarks concern Tarok noun-class tone raising only.
